_doc: PATH MATRIX for the guided online N-400 — how the page set varies by eligibility basis and marital status. Draft 13370795, 2026-07-30. Each row was SET and COMMITTED with Next, then the sidebar was re-read. This is the last open piece of the capture. Nothing was Submitted, Signed or Paid.

ELIGIBILITY_BASIS_MATRIX.method: For each of the six eligibility codes: set the radio, commit with Next, re-read every sidebar href. All six measured back to back under otherwise identical answers, so these ARE comparable.

193.label: Spouse of USC in qualified employment outside the US

194.label: Military service during a period of hostilities

190.label: At least one year of honorable military service at any time

KEY_TAKEAWAYS: VAWA (189), General (191) and Other (195) add NO pages at all — they are structurally identical to each other.
The two MILITARY codes (190, 194) are structurally identical to each other and add three military evidence pages.
192 and 193 SHARE /evidence/your-current-spouse-us-citizenship but differ in their second page (evidence-about-your-marriage vs current-spouse-qualifying-employment).

So eligibility basis affects ONLY which evidence/upload pages are offered. It never changes a typed page. That means the backend map's field side needs no eligibility branching at all — only upload_pages does.
ELIGIBILITY_BASIS_MATRIX.N426_NOTE: /evidence/form-n426-request-for-certification-of-military-or-naval-service is a slot for Form N-426 (Request for Certification of Military or Naval Service) — a separate USCIS form the firm would have to produce. We do not generate N-426 today, and the military bases are not in our case-type model, so this is out of scope but worth recording.

MARITAL_STATUS_MATRIX.method: All six status codes set and committed. CAVEAT: this sweep ran with eligibility=191, whereas the earlier Married/Divorced readings were taken under eligibility=192. So compare the DELTAS below, not raw totals across the two sweeps.

1.label: Single, never married
1.note: FEWEST pages of any status. numberOfTimesMarried is not even rendered, and two evidence pages drop away (the marriage-certificate slot and child-and-spousal-support).

2.label: Married
2.note: The ONLY status that reveals the current-spouse pages. Also the only one that adds /evidence/child-and-spousal-support.

MARITAL_STATUS_MATRIX.SURPRISE: SEPARATED (7) does NOT reveal the current-spouse pages, even though a separated applicant still has a spouse. Only MARRIED (2) does. If the firm expects spouse details to be filed for a separated client, the online form simply does not ask for them.
MARITAL_STATUS_MATRIX.PRIOR_MARRIAGE_NOW_CONCLUSIVE: All SIX marital statuses were tested, several with numberOfTimesMarried=2 committed. NOT ONE produces prior-marriage typed fields. Combined with the earlier spouse-side test, this confirms: the online N-400 collects prior-marriage substance ONLY as documents, via /evidence/current-marriage-certificate-and-previous-marriage-documents. The paper N-400 does have those fields, so this is a genuine paper-vs-online capability gap — facts we hold for the PDF have nowhere to go online. A mapping decision, not an extension bug.

OCCUPATION_IS_A_CLOSED_LIST.kind: MUI Autocomplete — closed list, NOT free text
options: Occupations in Data Communications and Networks
Wholesale and Retail Trade Managers and Officials
Wholesale and Retail Trade Managers and Officials
OCCUPATION_IS_A_CLOSED_LIST.THIS_IS_A_REAL_MAPPING_PROBLEM: Our fact applicant.employment_education_history[i].occupation_or_field is FREE TEXT (a client types 'Software Engineer'). The online form will only accept one of these 29 categories. So the backend needs a free-text -> category classifier, and the edge cases are judgement calls, not string matching. 'Occupation Not Reported/Unknown/Invalid' exists as a fallback but using it silently would degrade a filing.
OCCUPATION_IS_A_CLOSED_LIST.USCIS_BUG: 'Wholesale and Retail Trade Managers and Officials' appears TWICE in the live list. 29 entries, 28 distinct. An exact-match picker will hit the first, which is fine — but a uniqueness assertion over the option list would fail.
OCCUPATION_IS_A_CLOSED_LIST.punctuation_warning: Several entries carry commas, slashes, colons and periods ('I.T. Software Development', 'Editors: Publication, Broadcast, and Script'). Byte-exact matching required.
